course_name_original: Atatürk İlkeleri ve İnkılap Tarihi I
course_name_en: Atatürk's Principles and History of the Revolution I

learning_outcomes.text: Explains ways to access historical information and how historical sources should be evaluated.
Evaluates the continuities and discontinuities between Ottoman modernization and the Turkish Revolution.
Analyzes the effects of the Italo-Turkish War, Balkan Wars, and World War I on the Ottoman Empire.
Explains the occupations that emerged after the Armistice of Mudros and the conditions for the emergence of the National Struggle.
Evaluates Mustafa Kemal Pasha's political leadership and organizational strategy during the National Struggle.
Explains the relationship between the Amasya, Erzurum, and Sivas processes and Misak-ı Millî (National Pact).

syllabus_topics: Necessity of studying Atatürk's Principles and History of the Revolution. Concepts of revolution, reform, Tanzimat, constitutional monarchy, coup, and republic.
Developments in Europe: Industrial Revolution, French Revolution, and their effects on the Ottoman Empire.
Renovation movements in the Ottoman Empire: Tanzimat, Islahat (Reform), and Constitutional Monarchy period developments.
Intellectual currents that emerged in the Ottoman Empire.
The process leading to World War I: Italo-Turkish War, Balkan Wars, the Eastern Question, and modern colonialism.
The Ottoman Empire's entry into World War I and the fronts.
The Ottoman Empire and the world in World War I.
Post-World War I developments, Armistice of Mudros, and Anatolian occupations.
Transition to the National Struggle period: occupations, initial reactions, and general assessment.
National Struggle preparation period, associations, Kuvayi Milliye (National Forces), Mustafa Kemal's stance against occupations, and his emergence as a leader.
Circulars and congresses published during the National Struggle period, opening of the Last Ottoman Assembly of Representatives, and Misak-ı Millî (National Pact).
Opening of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey, revolts against the opening of the Assembly, and measures taken.
Armistice of Mudanya and Treaty of Lausanne.
assessment_rules: The midterm exam contributes 40% to the final grade, and the final exam contributes 60%. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate and specified in the academic calendar.
